title: limonium graecum subsp. divaricatum
intro: Limonium graecum subsp. divaricatum, commonly known as Divaricate Sea Lavender, is a plant species within the Plumbaginaceae family. It is a succulent perennial herb with a rich history of traditional use in folk medicine, valued for its potential health benefits and therapeutic actions. The bioactive constituents of Divaricate Sea Lavender include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenes, which are believed to contribute to its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. Research suggests that this plant may have therapeutic actions such as wound healing, antioxidant protection, and anti-inflammatory effects, although further studies are needed to confirm its efficacy.
